findings.title: The promised invariant test cannot falsify its invariant: `fc.string()` never draws a name in the RepWorth sequence, so a `return 'RepWorth'` implementation passes it
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured, not inferred. (1) With `nextFactorFriendlyName` replaced by `return 'RepWorth';` the test passes (rt-1149-04). (2) Over 100,000 draws of the shipped arbitrary `fc.array(fc.option(fc.string(), { nil: null }), { maxLength: 20 })`, ZERO generated arrays contained the literal 'RepWorth'; the suite runs fast-check's default 100. (3) The same mutant is killed in 7 draws by a domain-shaped arbitrary (`fc.oneof(fc.constantFrom('RepWorth','RepWorth 2','RepWorth 3','Laptop'), fc.option(fc.string(), { nil: null }))`), which still passes against the real implementation over 2,000 draws. The house-style reference the intake cites (`src/lib/reviews/__tests__/sentiment.test.ts:46`) uses a domain-shaped arbitrary (`fc.option(fc.double(...))` over the real rating domain) precisely so the branches are reached. Behavioural replacement: draw names from the RepWorth sequence alongside arbitrary strings, keeping the same assertion.

findings.title: Provider-controlled enrollment error text now reaches `isStepUpRequiredError`'s /sign in again/i sniff, which can attach a 'Verify with your authenticator' link to an enrollment failure
findings.reason: Before this branch the enrollment failure string was the fixed constant 'Could not start MFA enrollment.', so the regex at src/app/(authenticated)/settings/security/SecuritySections.tsx:42 could never match it. The new unmapped branch interpolates the raw Supabase message into that same string, and SecurityClient.tsx:71 feeds the hook's `error` straight into `SecurityErrorNotice`, which renders the STEP_UP_HREF link whenever the sentence matches /sign in again/i. Whether Supabase Auth ever emits an enroll-path message containing that phrase was NOT verified in this pass (offline), so this is recorded as a coupling the diff creates with no test over it, not a proven defect. Cheapest fix: key the step-up link off a sentinel the hook sets, not off the sentence text.
